refnamediv.refpurpose: Enable/disable asynchronous signal handling or return the old setting

refentry.refsect1:
&reftitle.returnvalues;
When used as getter (enable parameter is &null;) it returns whether asynchronous signal handling is enabled. When used as setter (enable parameter is not &null;), it returns whether asynchronous signal handling was enabled before the function call.

&reftitle.notes;
With asynchronous signal handling enabled, a handler installed with pcntl_signal is not called at the moment the signal is received. The signal is recorded, and the handler is called the next time the engine checks for pending signals while executing PHP code, for instance after a function call returns, or on the next iteration of a loop.
As a consequence, a long-running call to an internal function, such as curl_exec or a database query, is not interrupted to call the handler: the handler is only called once that function returns. The handler is called earlier only if the function calls back into PHP code while it runs, for instance through a CURLOPT_XFERINFOFUNCTION callback.
A signal may still interrupt a system call the function is blocked in. For instance, sleep then returns early, and the handler is called once it has returned.
